claims.statement: In Turkic mythology Tepegöz is a one-eyed ogre with an eye on his forehead, a kind of cyclops, appearing in the Book of Dede Korkut, a famous epic of the Oghuz Turks.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Tepegöz adalah raksasa bermata satu di dahi, semacam kiklop, yang muncul dalam Kitab Dede Korkut, epos terkenal bangsa Turk Oghuz.
claims.quote: In Turkic mythology, Tepegoz or Tepegöz is a legendary creature who has only one eye on his forehead – a kind of cyclops. He is an ogre that appears in the Book of Dede Korkut, a famous epic story of the Oghuz Turks.

claims.statement: In Turkic languages tepe means high or hill and goz means eye; the round opening at the top of a yurt is also called a tepegoz.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Turkik, tepe berarti tinggi atau bukit dan goz berarti mata; lubang bundar di puncak yurt juga disebut tepegoz.
claims.quote: In Turkic languages, tepe means high/hill, and goz means eye. The circular opening at the top of a yurt or ger is also called a tepegoz.

claims.statement: In the story an Oghuz herdsman sees a nymph who later gives birth, and finds the monstrous infant, a lump of flesh.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisahnya, seorang gembala Oghuz melihat seorang peri yang kemudian melahirkan, dan menemukan bayi mengerikan berupa gumpalan daging.
claims.quote: Years later a herdsman of the Oghuz saw a nymph who gave birth days later. The herdsman finds the monstrous infant, a fleshly thing.

claims.statement: Another source glosses tepe as forehead, so Tepegöz means "eye on the forehead".
claims.statement_id: Sumber lain mengartikan tepe sebagai dahi, sehingga Tepegöz berarti "mata di dahi".
claims.quote: In den Turksprachen bedeutet tepe/təpə „Stirn“ und goz/göz bedeutet „Auge“, also Tepegöz „Auge auf der Stirn“

claims.statement: The core of its story: Tepegöz drives a man into his cave to eat him, but the man blinds his single eye with a sharp point and escapes wrapped in a sheepskin.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya pada intinya: Tepegöz menggiring seseorang ke guanya untuk dimakan, tetapi orang itu membutakannya dengan menusuk matanya yang tunggal, lalu lolos dengan berselubung kulit domba.
claims.quote: одноглазый великан (дэв) в тюркской мифологии, рассказ о котором сводится к тому, что Тепегёз загоняет человека в пещеру, своё логово, собираясь съесть, но человек ослепляет его, вонзив в его единственный глаз остриё, и выбирается из пещеры, накинув на себя овечью шкуру.

claims.statement: The three-headed eagle is a mythological or heraldic eagle, an augmented version of the double-headed eagle.
claims.statement_id: Elang berkepala tiga adalah elang mitologis atau heraldik, semacam versi tambahan dari elang berkepala dua.
claims.quote: The three-headed eagle, also called triple-headed eagle, is a mythological or heraldic eagle, as it were an augmented version of the double-headed eagle.

claims.statement: A three-headed eagle appears in the apocryphal Latin Ezra, in a dream of the high priest Ezra.
claims.statement_id: Elang berkepala tiga disebut dalam kitab apokrif Ezra Latin, dalam mimpi imam besar Ezra.
claims.quote: A three-headed eagle is mentioned in the apocryphal Latin Ezra, featuring in a dream by the high priest Ezra.

claims.statement: In a Chechen fairy tale a three-headed eagle is a monstrous foe the hero must kill.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng Chechnya, elang berkepala tiga menjadi lawan mengerikan yang harus dibunuh sang pahlawan.
claims.quote: In a Chechen fairy tale, a three-headed eagle figures as a monstrous adversary to be killed by the hero.

claims.statement: Öksökö is an eagle with two or three heads in Yakut and Dolgan folklore.
claims.statement_id: Öksökö adalah nama elang berkepala dua atau tiga dalam cerita rakyat Yakut dan Dolgan.
claims.quote: Öksökö (Өксөку) is the name of an eagle with either two or three heads in Yakut and Dolgan folklore.

claims.statement: A three-headed eagle is shown as the arms of minnesinger Reinmar von Zweter (c. 1200–1248) in the Codex Manesse (c. 1300).
claims.statement_id: Elang berkepala tiga tampil sebagai lambang penyanyi minnesang Reinmar von Zweter (sekitar 1200–1248) dalam Codex Manesse (sekitar 1300).
claims.quote: is shown as the coat of arms of minnesinger Reinmar von Zweter (c. 1200–1248) in the Codex Manesse (c. 1300).

claims.statement: The sceptre of Tsar Michael I of Russia was decorated with a three-headed eagle.
claims.statement_id: Tongkat kerajaan Tsar Mikhail I dari Rusia dihiasi elang berkepala tiga.
claims.quote: The sceptre of tsar Michael I of Russia was decorated with a three-headed eagle

claims.statement: In heraldry the three-headed eagle is a rare charge.
claims.statement_id: Dalam heraldik, elang berkepala tiga adalah hewan lambang yang langka.
claims.quote: Der Dreiköpfige Adler, auch mit Dreifachadler bezeichnet, ist ein seltenes Wappentier in der Heraldik.

claims.statement: The text describes an eagle with twelve feathered wings and three heads rising from the sea.
claims.statement_id: Kitab itu menyebut seekor elang dengan dua belas sayap berbulu dan tiga kepala naik dari laut.
claims.quote: поднялся с моря орёл, у которого было двенадцать крыльев пернатых и три головы

claims.statement: The Barmanou is a bipedal humanoid primate cryptid said to inhabit the mountains of northern Afghanistan and Pakistan.
claims.statement_id: Barmanou adalah kriptid primata mirip manusia berjalan dua kaki yang konon menghuni pegunungan Afganistan utara dan Pakistan.
claims.quote: is a bipedal humanoid primate cryptid that is said to inhabit the mountainous region of northern Afghanistan and Pakistan.

claims.statement: The Barmanou is analogous to North America's Bigfoot; the term comes from Khowar and is now used in Urdu, Shina, Pashto and Kashmiri.
claims.statement_id: Barmanou sepadan dengan Bigfoot di Amerika Utara; istilahnya berasal dari bahasa Khowar dan kini dipakai dalam bahasa Urdu, Shina, Pashto, dan Kashmir.
claims.quote: The Barmanou is analogous to the Bigfoot of North America. The term Barmanou originates in Khowar, but is now used in several Afghan and Pakistani languages including Urdu, Shina, Pashto, and Kashmiri.

claims.statement: Its supposed range covers the Chitral and Karakoram ranges, between the Pamirs and the Himalayas.
claims.statement_id: Wilayah jelajahnya diduga meliputi Pegunungan Chitral dan Karakoram, di antara Pamir dan Himalaya.
claims.quote: The proposed range of the Barmanou covers the Chitral and Karakoram Ranges, between the Pamirs and the Himalayas.

claims.statement: The Barmanou allegedly has human and ape traits, is known for abducting women, and is said to wear animal skins on its back and head.
claims.statement_id: Barmanou konon berciri manusia sekaligus kera, terkenal menculik perempuan, dan dilaporkan memakai kulit binatang di punggung dan kepalanya.
claims.quote: The Barmanou allegedly possesses both human and apelike characteristics, and has a reputation for abducting women and attempting to mate with them. It is also reported to wear animal skins upon its back and head.

claims.statement: One source derives the name from Sanskrit bar-manu, "hairy man".
claims.statement_id: Satu sumber menurunkan namanya dari bahasa Sanskerta bar-manu, "manusia berbulu".
claims.quote: Le Barmanou ou Barmanu (du sanskrit Bar-manu, homme poilu)

claims.statement: Zoologist Jordi Magraner gathered dozens of testimonies from 1988 to 1990 and published an article on it in 1994.
claims.statement_id: Ahli zoologi Jordi Magraner mengumpulkan puluhan kesaksian dari 1988 hingga 1990 dan menerbitkan artikel tentangnya pada 1994.
claims.quote: Il fut l'objet d'une étude par le zoologiste Jordi Magraner qui recueillit plusieurs dizaines de témoignages de 1988 à 1990 et publia en 1994 un article à ce sujet.

claims.statement: Bichura is a house spirit in Turkic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Bichura adalah roh rumah dalam mitologi Turkik.
claims.quote: is a house spirit in Turkic mythology.

claims.statement: Bichura is also said to take the form of cats or dogs.
claims.statement_id: Bichura juga dikatakan dapat menjelma kucing atau anjing.
claims.quote: It has also been said that Bichura can take on the appearance of cats or dogs.

claims.statement: Its doings vaguely resemble a poltergeist's and are not necessarily harmful; it wears red clothes.
claims.statement_id: Tingkahnya agak mirip poltergeist dan tidak selalu merugikan; ia memakai pakaian merah.
claims.quote: The actions performed by a Bichura vaguely resemble those of poltergeists and are not necessarily harmful. It wears red dresses.

claims.statement: Traditionally every house has a Bichura; it pulls hair to warn a woman of an abusive man and moans and howls to warn of trouble.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi setiap rumah punya Bichura; ia menarik rambut untuk memperingatkan perempuan akan lelaki kasar, serta mengerang dan melolong sebagai tanda bahaya.
claims.quote: Traditionally, every house is said to have a Bichura. He would pull hair to warn a woman of danger from an abusive man. He would moan and howl to warn of coming trouble.

claims.statement: If it shows itself, death is coming; if it weeps, someone in the family will die.
claims.statement_id: Bila ia menampakkan diri, itu pertanda kematian; bila ia menangis, akan ada kematian dalam keluarga.
claims.quote: If he showed himself, it forewarned of death, and if he was weeping it was said to be a death in the family.

claims.statement: If Bichura is unhappy, it plays nasty tricks on the household.
claims.statement_id: Bila Bichura tidak senang, ia mengusili penghuni rumah.
claims.quote: If Bichura becomes unhappy, it plays nasty tricks on the members of the household.

claims.statement: Bichura is a mythical being of Tatar tales and myths, a house spirit.
claims.statement_id: Bichura adalah makhluk mitos dalam dongeng dan mitos Tatar, sejenis roh penunggu rumah.
claims.quote: мифическое существо татарских сказок и мифов, домовой

claims.statement: The word may derive from Old Turkic bičin, "monkey".
claims.statement_id: Kata ini mungkin berasal dari kata Turkik Kuno bičin, "kera".
claims.quote: Возможно, слово восходит к древнетюркскому bičin (бичин) — обезьяна.

claims.statement: Tatars pictured the bichura as a small woman in an old-fashioned headdress, living under the floor of houses or in bathhouses.
claims.statement_id: Orang Tatar membayangkan bichura sebagai perempuan bertubuh kecil dengan penutup kepala kuno, yang tinggal di bawah lantai rumah atau di pemandian.
claims.quote: У татар бичура представлялись в образе женщины маленького роста в старинном головном уборе. Считалось, что они могли поселяться в домах под полом или в банях.

claims.statement: Unlike the oy iyase, bichura did not live in every house.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari oy iyase, bichura tidak tinggal di setiap rumah.
claims.quote: В отличие от ой иясе бичура жили не во всех домах.

claims.statement: Chai nenesi is a name for Turkic water spirits, usually of creeks; she sucks people into swamps and lakes and kills animals standing by still water.
claims.statement_id: Chai nenesi adalah sebutan bagi roh air Turkik, biasanya di sungai kecil; ia mengisap orang ke rawa dan danau serta membunuh hewan yang berdiri dekat air tenang.
claims.quote: is a name applied to Turkic spirits of water, commonly creeks. She is responsible for sucking people into swamps and lakes as well as killing the animals standing near the still waters.

claims.statement: She is described as a white, naked woman with tousled hair who harasses people and brings misfortune to drunkards.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan putih telanjang berambut kusut yang mengganggu orang dan membawa sial bagi pemabuk.
claims.quote: She is described as a white nude female with tousled [hair] and is known to harass people and bring misfortune to drunkards.

claims.statement: In most versions she is a restless being tied to the "unclean force"; at night she leaves the water to climb a tree and sing, or sits on a dock combing her hair.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebanyakan versi ia makhluk gelisah yang dikaitkan dengan "kekuatan najis"; pada malam hari ia keluar dari air untuk memanjat pohon dan bernyanyi, atau duduk di dermaga menyisir rambut.
claims.quote: In most versions, Chai Nenesi is an unquiet being, associated with the "unclean force". She Usually comes out of the water at night to climb a tree and sing songs or sit on a dock and comb her hair.

claims.statement: Çay nənəsi is a mythical water being in Turkic and Azerbaijani mythology.
claims.statement_id: Çay nənəsi adalah makhluk mitos yang berhubungan dengan air dalam mitologi Turki dan Azerbaijan.
claims.quote: Çay nənəsi — türk və Azərbaycan mifologiyasında su ilə bağlı mifik varlıq.

claims.statement: In the Azerbaijani source, Çay nənəsi has the form of a beautiful old woman.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber Azerbaijan, Çay nənəsi berwujud perempuan tua yang cantik.
claims.quote: Çay nənəsi gözəl yaşlı qadın cildindədir.

claims.statement: She has black or yellow hair long enough to reach the ground, large breasts and no eyebrows.
claims.statement_id: Rambutnya hitam atau kuning sepanjang hingga menyentuh tanah, payudaranya besar, dan ia tidak beralis.
claims.quote: Onun yerə çatacaq qədər uzun qara və ya sarı saçları var, məmələri böyükdür, qaşı yoxdur.

claims.statement: Äbädä is a harmless forest spirit of Turkic mythology that looks like an old woman and also appears in the mythologies of Siberian peoples.
claims.statement_id: Äbädä adalah roh hutan yang tidak berbahaya dalam mitologi Turkik, berwujud perempuan tua, dan juga dikenal dalam mitologi bangsa-bangsa Siberia.
claims.quote: is an innocent forest spirit in Turkic mythology. It looks like an old woman. Äbädä also is represented in mythologies of Siberian peoples.

claims.statement: The same source also calls it a protector of the forest's birds, trees and animals, appearing as a blue-skinned human with two great horns, green hair and beard, carrying a club or whip.
claims.statement_id: Sumber yang sama juga menyebutnya pelindung burung, pohon, dan hewan hutan yang berwujud manusia berkulit biru, bertanduk dua besar, berambut dan berjanggut hijau, serta membawa gada atau cambuk.
claims.quote: He protects the birds, trees, and animals of the forest; he appears in the shape of a human with blue skin, two great horns, green hair, and a long green beard across his face, carrying a club or whip indicating his mastery of the forest.

claims.statement: Anyone who meets an Äbädä must thwart it at once by turning all their clothes inside out and backwards and swapping their shoes.
claims.statement_id: Bila bertemu Äbädä, orang harus segera menangkalnya dengan membalik semua pakaian dan menukar sepatu kiri-kanan.
claims.quote: Should one ever encounter an Äbädä, one must thwart him immediately by turning all one's clothes inside out and backwards, and placing one's shoes on the opposite feet.

claims.statement: In Turkic and Tatar mythology Əbədə is a tree spirit that lives in forests, harms no one and looks like an old woman.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Turki dan Tatar, Əbədə adalah jin pohon yang tinggal di hutan, tidak mencelakai manusia, dan berwujud perempuan tua.
claims.quote: Əbədə — türk və tatar mifologiyasında ağac cini. Meşələrdə yaşayır. İnsanlara zərər verməz. Yaşlı bir qadın görümündədir.

claims.statement: The rustling of dry leaves on the forest floor is the sound of her footsteps.
claims.statement_id: Gemeresik daun kering di tanah hutan adalah suara langkah kakinya.
claims.quote: Meşələrdə yerlərdəki qurumuş ağac yarpaqlarından gələn çıtırtılar onun ayaq səsləridir.

claims.statement: Its name is linked to the word ebe, meaning old woman.
claims.statement_id: Namanya terkait kata ebe yang berarti perempuan tua.
claims.quote: Ebe sözcüyü yaşlı qadın mənasındadır.

claims.statement: Ayaz Ata is a winter god from Tengrism and a tale character who serves as the Turkic counterpart of Santa Claus and Ded Moroz.
claims.statement_id: Ayaz Ata adalah dewa musim dingin dari Tengrisme sekaligus tokoh dongeng yang menjadi padanan Turkik bagi Sinterklas dan Ded Moroz.
claims.quote: Ayaz Ata is a winter god originating from Tengrism and a fictional tale character that serves as the Turkic counterpart to Santa Claus and Ded Moroz.

claims.statement: The name literally means Frost Father, though it is often translated Grandfather Frost.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan harfiah namanya adalah "Bapak Embun Beku", meski sering diterjemahkan "Kakek Embun Beku".
claims.quote: The literal translation of the name would be Frost Father, although the name is often translated as Grandfather Frost.

claims.statement: In Turkic mythology he was made from moonlight, brings cold weather and snow, protects people from excessive cold and "wakes nature from its sleep".
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitologi Turkik, ia tercipta dari cahaya bulan, membawa cuaca dingin dan salju, melindungi orang dari dingin yang berlebihan, dan "membangunkan alam dari tidurnya".
claims.quote: according to Turkic mythology is created of Moon light, caused by cold weather and associated with bringing snow, protecting people from too cold weather and "waking the nature up from its sleep".

claims.statement: Literary depictions usually show Ayaz Ata with Kar Kız.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggambaran sastra, Ayaz Ata biasanya ditemani Kar Kız.
claims.quote: Literary depictions of Ayaz Ata commonly show him accompanied by Kar Kız

claims.statement: Kar Kız is his granddaughter and helper, sometimes influenced by the Slavic Snegurochka.
claims.statement_id: Kar Kız adalah cucu dan pembantunya, kadang dipengaruhi tokoh Slavia Snegurochka.
claims.quote: his granddaughter and helper, sometimes with influence of Slavic Snegurochka

claims.statement: In Uzbek he is called Ayoz Bobo and in Turkmen Aýaz Baba.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Uzbek ia disebut Ayoz Bobo dan dalam bahasa Turkmen Aýaz Baba.
claims.quote: Ayaz Ata (usbekisch: Ayoz Bobo, kirgisisch: Аяз ата, kasachisch: Аяз Ата, turkmenisch: Aýaz Baba)

claims.statement: In Azerbaijani he is also known as Şaxta Baba.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Azerbaijan ia juga dikenal sebagai Şaxta Baba.
claims.quote: Azərbaycan türkcəsində "Şaxta Baba" olaraq da bilinir.

claims.statement: In various Turkic languages he is also named Ayas Xan or Ağ Ayas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam berbagai bahasa Turkik namanya juga Ayas Xan atau Ağ Ayas.
claims.quote: Müxtəlif Türk dillərində Ayas Xan və ya "Ağ Ayas" olaraq adı keçər.

claims.statement: Verechelen, or Chuvash dragons, are mythological dragons of Chuvash legend that can fly, breathe fire and change shape.
claims.statement_id: Verechelen atau naga Chuvash adalah naga mitologis dalam legenda orang Chuvash yang dapat terbang, menyemburkan api, dan berubah wujud.
claims.quote: also known as Chuvash dragons, are mythological dragons appearing in the legends of the Chuvash people. They are able to fly, breathe fire, and shapeshift.

claims.statement: The name means 'invisible snake'; these differ from Turkic counterparts such as Zilant, reflecting the mythology of Volga Bulgaria.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti "ular tak terlihat"; naga ini berbeda dari padanan Turkiknya seperti Zilant karena mencerminkan mitologi Bulgaria Volga.
claims.quote: The name means 'invisible snake'. These differ from their Turkic counterparts (such as Zilant), as they are said to reflect the mythology of Volga Bulgaria.

claims.statement: One kind is Věri Şělen, "fire snake", which like the Russian Gorynych has many heads and leaves a fiery trail in flight.
claims.statement_id: Satu jenisnya adalah Věri Şělen, "ular api", yang seperti Gorynych dari Rusia berkepala banyak dan meninggalkan jejak api saat terbang.
claims.quote: Chuvash dragon is Věri Şělen (Вӗри Ҫӗлен, lit. "fire snake"). Like the Russian Gorynych, the creature has multiple heads and leaves a fiery wake when flying.

claims.statement: In one legend the Bulgars found a big snake when founding Bilär; about to be killed, it begged for peace and asked Allah for wings, then flew away from Bilär.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu legenda, orang Bulgar menemukan ular besar saat mendirikan kota Bilär; ketika hendak dibunuh, ular itu memohon damai dan meminta sayap kepada Allah, lalu terbang meninggalkan Bilär.
claims.quote: According to one legend, when the Bulgars came to found the town of Bilär, they discovered a big snake living in the area. When they decided to kill it, the snake begged for peace and asked Allah to give him wings. Once he got wings, the snake flew away from Bilär.

claims.statement: In Chuvash mythology Verechelen is a fire serpent, a negative figure in legends that can turn into a human, often a dead spouse.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Chuvash, Verechelen adalah ular api, tokoh jahat dalam legenda yang dapat menjelma manusia, sering menyerupai suami atau istri yang telah meninggal.
claims.quote: существо в чувашской мифологии, представляющее собой огненного змея. В легендах оно описывается как отрицательный персонаж, способный превращаться в человека (зачастую в умершего супруга).

claims.statement: Religious scholar A. K. Salmin considers it mistaken to derive the name from věri şělen, "hot, fiery snake".
claims.statement_id: Ahli agama A. K. Salmin menganggap keliru penjelasan bahwa namanya berasal dari věri şělen, "ular panas, ular api".
claims.quote: Объяснение происхождения термина от чув. вӗри ҫӗлен («горячий, огненный змей») исследователь считает ошибочным

claims.statement: In Turkic mythology Hortdan (Hortlak) is the troubled soul of the dead rising from the grave.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Hortdan (Hortlak) adalah jiwa gelisah orang mati yang bangkit dari kubur.
claims.quote: In Turkic mythology, Hortdan (Turkish: Hortlak) is the troubled soul of the dead rising from the grave.

claims.statement: The Hortdan can turn into an animal, become invisible and drain victims' vitality through blood loss.
claims.statement_id: Hortdan dapat berubah menjadi hewan, menjadi tak terlihat, dan menguras tenaga korbannya lewat darah.
claims.quote: Some of the properties of the Hortdan include: the ability to transform into an animal, invisibility, and the propensity to drain the vitality of victims via blood loss.

claims.statement: Hortdans are creatures of Tatar folk mythology representing evil spirits, the spirits of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Hortdan adalah makhluk mitologi rakyat Tatar yang melambangkan roh jahat, roh orang mati.
claims.quote: The Hortdans are creatures of Tatar folk mythology, as a representation of evil spirits, the spirits of the dead.

claims.statement: Originally the Hortlak ghost was said to appear where murdered people's souls departed or human blood was shed, most often above the graves of the slain.
claims.statement_id: Awalnya hantu Hortlak konon muncul di tempat jiwa orang yang dibunuh pergi atau darah manusia tertumpah, dan paling sering terlihat di atas kubur korban pembunuhan.
claims.quote: Originally, the Hortlak ghost is said to "appear" where the souls of murdered people have departed or where human blood has been shed. However, people most often encounter the ghost above the graves of the slain.

claims.statement: In that original form it does not harm people; they only see it wandering or sitting, mournfully wailing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi awal itu ia tidak mencelakai orang; mereka hanya melihatnya berkeliaran atau duduk sambil merintih sedih.
claims.quote: It doesn't harm people; they only "see" it wandering or sitting there, mournfully making a sorrowful sound.

claims.statement: In Azerbaijani folklore the xortdan is a dreadful being that rises from the grave at night and sucks the blood of sleepers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Azerbaijan, xortdan adalah makhluk mengerikan yang bangkit dari kubur pada malam hari dan mengisap darah orang yang tidur.
claims.quote: Xortdan ya da xortlaq — gecə qəbirdən xortlayaraq çıxıb yatmış adamların qanını soran, onlara pislik edən qorxunc, dəhşətli mövhum bir vücud, folklor və xalq əfsanələrinə görə qaniçən məxluq.

claims.statement: In the best-known tradition, sunlight, an aspen stake through the heart, a silver bullet and a few other things kill it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi yang paling dikenal, xortdan dapat dibunuh dengan sinar matahari, pasak kayu aspen di jantung, peluru perak, dan beberapa hal lain.
claims.quote: Ən tanınmış ənənəyə görə onları günəş işığı, ürəyə vurulmuş ağcaqovaq payası, gümüş güllə və daha bir neçə şey öldürür.

claims.statement: In Turkic mythology Konrul is a long-lived bird that is cyclically regenerated or reborn, like a phoenix.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Konrul adalah burung berumur panjang yang terus-menerus beregenerasi atau lahir kembali, mirip phoenix.
claims.quote: is a long-lived bird that is cyclically regenerated or reborn, similar to a phoenix.

claims.statement: Konrul is pictured as a giant bird able to carry off an elephant, a peacock with a dog's head and lion's claws, sometimes with a human face.
claims.statement_id: Konrul digambarkan sebagai burung raksasa yang mampu membawa gajah, berwujud merak berkepala anjing dan bercakar singa, kadang berwajah manusia.
claims.quote: Konrul is depicted as a winged creature in the shape of a bird, gigantic enough to carry off an elephant. It appears as a peacock with the head of a dog and the claws of a lion; sometimes however also with a human face.

claims.statement: It is hostile to snakes and lives where there is plenty of water.
claims.statement_id: Ia bermusuhan dengan ular dan habitatnya tempat yang banyak air.
claims.quote: It has an enmity towards snakes and its natural habitat is a place with plenty of water.

claims.statement: Konrul has a twin named Toghrul.
claims.statement_id: Konrul memiliki kembaran bernama Toghrul.
claims.quote: Konrul also has a twin named "Toghrul"

claims.statement: In one tale a hero saves Konrul's young by killing a serpent climbing their tree; in reward Konrul gives him three feathers to burn when he needs help, and later carries him to a distant land.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, seorang pahlawan menyelamatkan anak-anak Konrul dengan membunuh ular yang memanjat pohon; sebagai hadiah Konrul memberinya tiga bulu untuk dibakar bila butuh pertolongan, lalu membawanya ke negeri jauh.
claims.quote: In one account a hero rescues Konrul's offspring by killing a serpent that was crawling up the tree to feed upon them. As a reward, Konrul gives him three of her feathers which the hero uses to call her for help by burning them. Later, Konrul carries him to a distant land.

claims.statement: In another, Konrul carries the hero out of the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah lain, Konrul membawa sang pahlawan keluar dari dunia bawah.
claims.quote: In another, Konrul carries the hero out of the netherworld.

claims.statement: Konrul is a long-lived bird that regenerates or is reborn cyclically, like the phoenix.
claims.statement_id: Konrul burung berumur panjang yang beregenerasi atau lahir kembali secara berkala, seperti phoenix.
claims.quote: est un oiseau de longue vie qui se régénère ou renaît cycliquement, comme le phénix.

claims.statement: Mhachkay is a creature of Turkic, especially Tatar, mythology somewhat like a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Mhachkay adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Turkik, terutama Tatar, yang agak mirip vampir.
claims.quote: is a creature in Turkic (especially Tatar) mythology which is somewhat similar to a vampire.

claims.statement: A person born with two hearts and two souls was thought to be a Mhachkay and, once recognised, was driven from human settlements.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang lahir dengan dua jantung dan dua jiwa dipercaya sebagai Mhachkay, dan bila dikenali ia diusir dari permukiman.
claims.quote: A person born with two hearts and two souls was believed to be a Mhachkay. When one was recognized it was chased away from human habitations.

claims.statement: Mhachkays were usually people who died young; only one soul departed, and the other revived the corpse to prey on the living.
claims.statement_id: Mhachkay biasanya orang yang mati muda; hanya satu jiwanya yang pergi, sedangkan jiwa lainnya menghidupkan jasadnya untuk memangsa makhluk hidup.
claims.quote: Mhachkays were usually people who died at a young age, but only one soul passed on, and the other soul caused the deceased Mhachkay to come alive and prey upon other living beings.

claims.statement: These undead fly at night as owls, attacking night travellers and people who stray into the woods, sucking their blood and eating their insides.
claims.statement_id: Mayat hidup ini terbang pada malam hari dalam wujud burung hantu, menyerang pejalan malam dan orang yang tersesat di hutan, mengisap darah dan memakan isi tubuh mereka.
claims.quote: These undead creatures fly at night in the form of an owl and attack night-time travelers and people who wander off into the woods, sucking out their blood and eating out their insides.

claims.statement: When a known Mhachkay dies, beheading the corpse and burying the head apart is said to stop it rising again.
claims.statement_id: Bila orang yang dikenal sebagai Mhachkay meninggal, memenggal jasadnya dan mengubur kepalanya terpisah dipercaya mencegahnya bangkit.
claims.quote: When a person recognized as a Mhachkay dies, decapitating the corpse and burying the head separate from the rest of the body is said to prevent a Mhachkay from rising back from the dead

claims.statement: Like Nosferatu, the məçkəy is believed to carry tağun, the plague.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Nosferatu, məçkəy dipercaya membawa penyakit tağun, yaitu wabah.
claims.quote: Məsələn eynilə Nosferatu nümunəsində olduğu kimi, "tağun" (yəni vəba) xəstəliyi daşıdığına inanılır.

claims.statement: It is imagined as a hunched old woman spreading death, sometimes an old man.
claims.statement_id: Ia dibayangkan sebagai perempuan tua bungkuk pembawa maut, kadang lelaki tua.
claims.quote: Ölüm saçan donqar bir yaşlı qadın (və ya bəzən yaşlı bir kişi) şəklində düşünülər.

claims.statement: In Mongolian məç means monkey, while məs means weapon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Mongol məç berarti kera, sedangkan məs berarti senjata.
claims.quote: Məç monqolcada meymun, Məs isə silah deməkdir.

claims.statement: Muu shuvuu is a mythological bird in Turkic and Mongolic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Muu shuvuu adalah burung mitologis dalam mitologi Turkik dan Mongol.
claims.quote: is a mythological bird in Turkic and, Mongolic mythology.

claims.statement: They look like young girls but have sharp beaks, hidden behind a veil or their hands, with which they suck their victims' blood.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tampak seperti gadis muda tetapi berparuh tajam yang ditutupi kerudung atau tangan, dan dengan paruh itu mereka mengisap darah korban.
claims.quote: They would look like young girls but have a sharp beak, which they try to cover either in a veil or with their hands. With their beaks, they would try to suck out the blood of the bodies of their victims.

claims.statement: They were especially dangerous to travellers and lone hunters.
claims.statement_id: Mereka terutama berbahaya bagi pejalan dan pemburu yang sendirian.
claims.quote: They were especially dangerous to travellers or lonely hunters.

claims.statement: A muu shuvuu is believed to arise when a girl dies young or violently; her soul then becomes a muu shuvuu.
claims.statement_id: Muu shuvuu dipercaya tercipta ketika seorang gadis mati muda atau mati dengan kekerasan; jiwanya lalu berubah menjadi muu shuvuu.
claims.quote: Muu shuvuu is believed to be usually created when a girl dies young or by violent death. The girl's soul would turn into a muu shuvuu then.

claims.statement: A father who hides a flint in his dead daughter's hand will also turn her soul into one.
claims.statement_id: Seorang ayah yang menyelipkan batu api di tangan putrinya yang meninggal juga akan mengubah jiwanya menjadi muu shuvuu.
claims.quote: When a father hides a flint in his deceased daughters hand, however, he would turn her soul into one as well.

claims.statement: In Buryat mythology Muu Shubuun is a demonic being in the form of an ugly bird of prey or carrion bird.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Buryat, Muu Shubuun adalah makhluk iblis berwujud burung buruk rupa, pemangsa, atau pemakan bangkai.
claims.quote: персонаж бурятской мифологии, демоническое существо в облике уродливой, хищной или падальной птицы.

claims.statement: In Buryat belief it personifies epidemics, sudden death, the evil eye and all kinds of misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Buryat ia personifikasi wabah, kematian mendadak, mata jahat, dan segala kemalangan.
claims.quote: В традиционных верованиях бурят Муу Шубуун выступает как персонификация эпидемий, внезапной смерти, сглаза и всевозможных несчастий.

claims.statement: Its name means "bad bird", "evil bird" or "bird of sickness".
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti "burung buruk", "burung jahat", atau "burung penyakit".
claims.quote: «дурная птица», «злая птица», «птица болезни»

claims.statement: Pitsen is a forest creature in the mythology of the Siberian Tatars.
claims.statement_id: Pitsen adalah makhluk hutan dalam mitologi Tatar Siberia.
claims.quote: is a forest creature in the Siberian Tatars' mythology.

claims.statement: Its role is contradictory: it can bring luck but also trouble, leading people into the wilderness.
claims.statement_id: Perannya bertentangan: ia bisa membawa keberuntungan, tetapi juga kesulitan dengan menyesatkan manusia ke belantara.
claims.quote: Pitsen's role is contradictory. It could bring luck, but also troubles, leading humans to the wilderness.

claims.statement: Pitsen often changes shape, appearing as an old man with staff and knapsack or as animals such as apes; it likes derelict lodges, riding horses and smearing their manes with tar.
claims.statement_id: Pitsen sering berubah wujud, misalnya menjadi orang tua bertongkat dan berbuntal atau hewan seperti kera; ia suka tinggal di pondok terbengkalai, menunggang kuda, dan mengolesi surai kuda dengan ter.
claims.quote: Shapeshifting is common for Pitsen: he may look like an elder with a staff and knapsack, but also like different animals, for example apes. Pitsen prefers to live in derelict lodges. He also likes to ride horses and to oil their mane with tar.

claims.statement: In one legend a hunter married a beautiful maiden met in the forest and grew rich, but coming home early he saw a tusked monster eating lizards; he cried out, and his wife and wealth vanished.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu legenda, seorang pemburu menikahi gadis cantik yang ditemuinya di hutan dan menjadi kaya, tetapi suatu hari ia pulang lebih awal dan melihat monster bergading memakan kadal; ia menjerit, dan istri serta kekayaannya lenyap.
claims.quote: One legend says that one hunter happened upon beautiful damsel in a forest and married her. Soon they become rich. Once he came home ahead of time and saw a tusky monster eating lizards. He cried, being horrified, and that moment his wife and his riches disappeared.

claims.statement: Pitsen is a counterpart of the Chuvash Arçuri and the Volga-Ural Tatar Şüräle.
claims.statement_id: Pitsen padanan Arçuri dari Chuvash dan Şüräle dari Tatar Volga-Ural.
claims.quote: Pitsen is a counterpart of Chuvash Arçuri and Volga-Ural Tatar Şüräle.

claims.statement: In Siberian Tatar mythology Pitsen is the spirit-master of the forest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Tatar Siberia, Pitsen adalah roh penguasa hutan.
claims.quote: в мифологии сибирских татар дух-хозяин леса.

claims.statement: Pitsen is also called bichen, pichan, pechan, pitsin, en, enperi or urman iyase.
claims.statement_id: Pitsen juga disebut bichen, pichan, pechan, pitsin, en, enperi, atau urman iyase.
claims.quote: также бичен, пичан, печан, пицин, ен, енпери, урман иясе

claims.statement: In Turkic folklore Abzar iyesi is a household spirit, the protector of the courtyard.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Turkik, Abzar iyesi adalah roh rumah tangga, pelindung halaman rumah.
claims.quote: is a household spirit. It is the protector spirit of courtyard.

claims.statement: The word iye means owner, master or possessor.
claims.statement_id: Kata iye berarti pemilik atau tuan.
claims.quote: The word "İye" means owner, master or possessor

claims.statement: It was linked with the farmyard, cattle shed and stable, like the house spirit Ev iyesi but less benevolent.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan pekarangan, kandang ternak, dan istal, mirip roh rumah Ev iyesi tetapi kurang baik hati.
claims.quote: It was associated with a farmstead's grounds, cattle shed, and stable. It is similar to the house spirit Ev iyesi, though it was less benevolent.

claims.statement: Abzar iyesi was thought more dangerous than Ev iyesi because it could threaten livestock, especially white-furred animals.
claims.statement_id: Abzar iyesi dianggap lebih berbahaya daripada Ev iyesi karena dapat mengancam ternak, terutama yang berbulu putih.
claims.quote: Abzar iyesi was considered more dangerous than Ev iyesi as it could pose a threat to livestock, particularly animals with white fur.

claims.statement: Abzar Ana is the female form of Abzar iyesi.
claims.statement_id: Abzar Ana adalah wujud perempuan Abzar iyesi.
claims.quote: Abzar Ana is female form of Abzar iyesi.

claims.statement: Abzar Ata is the male form of Abzar iyesi.
claims.statement_id: Abzar Ata adalah wujud lelaki Abzar iyesi.
claims.quote: Abzar Ata is male form of Abzar iyesi.

claims.statement: At night the abzar iyase sometimes appears as a person or an animal; it loves and feeds some livestock but persecutes others.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari abzar iyase kadang menampakkan diri sebagai manusia atau hewan; ia menyayangi dan memberi makan sebagian ternak, tetapi menyiksa yang lain.
claims.quote: Считалось, что по ночам абзар иясё иногда показывается в облике человека или какого-либо животного. Некоторых домашних животных он любит, кормит, а других — преследует.

claims.statement: As with a house spirit, one must stay on good terms with the abzar iyase, please it and now and then appease it.
claims.statement_id: Seperti roh rumah, abzar iyase harus dijaga hubungan baiknya, disenangkan, dan sesekali diberi persembahan.
claims.quote: Как и с домовым, с Абзар иясе нужно соблюдать хорошие отношения, угождать ему и временами умилостивлять

claims.statement: In Turkic folklore an Irshi (İrşi) is a fairy-like mythical being in the form of a spirit, often described as supernatural.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Turkik, Irshi (İrşi) adalah makhluk mitos mirip peri yang berwujud roh dan sering disebut gaib.
claims.quote: In Turkic folklore, an Irshi (Turkish: İrşi) is a type of mythical being or legendary fairy-like creature which is in a form of a spirit, often described as supernatural or preternatural.

claims.statement: The Irshi is usually described as a beautiful girl with magical powers.
claims.statement_id: Irshi biasanya digambarkan berwujud gadis cantik dan memiliki kekuatan sihir.
claims.quote: Irshi is generally described as human (beautiful girl) appearance and having magical powers.

claims.statement: She is depicted as kind, gentle and sweet, youthful and elegant, a superb dancer, and unable to lie.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan baik hati, lembut, dan manis, muda dan anggun, pandai menari, serta tidak bisa berbohong.
claims.quote: She is depicted as kind, gentle and sweet. They are youthful and elegant, and superb in the art of dancing. Irshi cannot lie.

claims.statement: Various animals have also been called Irshi, sometimes because these fairies change shape.
claims.statement_id: Berbagai hewan juga disebut Irshi, kadang karena peri ini berubah wujud.
claims.quote: Various animals have also been described as Irshi. Sometimes this is the result of shape shifting on part of this fairies.

claims.statement: In many legends the Irshi kidnaps humans, either babies, leaving changelings in their place, or young men.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak legenda Irshi suka menculik manusia, baik bayi yang diganti dengan anak tukaran maupun pemuda.
claims.quote: In many legends, the Irshi is prone to kidnapping humans, either as babies, leaving changelings in their place, or as young men

claims.statement: In Turkic and Altai folk belief the İrşi is a fairy, a bodiless female being.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Turki dan Altai, İrşi adalah peri, makhluk perempuan tanpa tubuh.
claims.quote: İrşi - türk və altay xalq inancında və xalq mədəniyyətində pəri. Cisimsiz dişi varlıq.

claims.statement: It takes the guise of a very beautiful girl, though in truth it has no eyes, ears, nose or hair; in tales they marry the heroes.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjelma gadis yang sangat cantik, padahal sebenarnya tidak bermata, bertelinga, berhidung, atau berambut; dalam dongeng mereka menikahi para pahlawan.
claims.quote: Çox gözəl qız bir qılığına bürünür. Lakin əslində nə gözü, nə qulağı, nə burnu, nə saçı olmayan bir canlıdır. Nağıl qəhrəmanı igidlərlə evlənərlər.

claims.statement: In Turkic mythology a Sazakan is a dragon, hawk, falcon or fiery dwarf that becomes a whirlwind and causes storms.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Sazakan adalah naga, elang, alap-alap, atau kurcaci api yang menjelma angin puting beliung dan menimbulkan badai.
claims.quote: In Turkic mythology, a Sazakan is a dragon, hawk, falcon, or fiery dwarf who turns himself into a whirlwind and causes storms.

claims.statement: Sazakan is a spirit that brings rain and hail; its influence can be good, giving rain useful for farming, or bad, bringing drought, downpours or hail.
claims.statement_id: Sazakan roh pembawa hujan dan hujan es; pengaruhnya bisa baik, memberi hujan yang bermanfaat bagi pertanian, atau buruk, berupa kekeringan, hujan deras, atau hujan es.
claims.quote: Sazakan is a spirit associated with bringing rain and hail. His influence on these precipitations can be positive, resulting with the amount of rain beneficial for agriculture, or negative, with a drought, downpours, or hail.

claims.statement: Sazakans also command the wind, which they use to strengthen storms.
claims.statement_id: Sazakan juga menguasai angin untuk memperkuat badai.
claims.quote: Sazakans also have power over wind, which they use to intensify storms.

claims.statement: Sazakans live around hills, mountains and high mounds, in the wilderness and sometimes in the clouds; in Nogai folklore they are noisy spirits and patrons of the clouds.
claims.statement_id: Sazakan tinggal di sekitar bukit, gunung, gundukan tinggi, belantara, dan kadang di awan; dalam cerita rakyat Nogai mereka roh yang riuh dan pelindung awan.
claims.quote: Sazakans live around hills, mountains, and high mounds; in the wilderness; and sometimes in the clouds. In Nogai folklore, Sazakans are described as being noisy spirits, and are the patron of the clouds.

claims.statement: In Turkic and Altai belief Sazakan is the storm jinn that roams the clouds in summer and appears before the rain in spring.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Turki dan Altai, Sazakan adalah jin badai yang berkeliaran di antara awan pada musim panas dan muncul sebelum hujan pada musim semi.
claims.quote: Sazakan – Türk ve Altay halk inancında ve mitolojisinde Kasırga Cini. Yaz mevsiminde bulutların arasında dolaşır. Baharda yağmurdan önce ortaya çıkar.

claims.statement: It is a huge, dragon-like being with branching horns.
claims.statement_id: Ia makhluk besar mirip naga dengan tanduk bercabang.
claims.quote: Ejderhaya benzeyen kocaman bir varlıktır. Budaklı boynuzları vardır.

claims.statement: When an unexpected snowstorm or sudden downpour strikes, people say "Sazakan is playing".
claims.statement_id: Bila badai salju atau hujan deras datang tiba-tiba, orang berkata "Sazakan sedang bermain".
claims.quote: Hiç beklenmedik bir kar fırtınası ve tipi bastırırsa veya aniden sağanak yağmur başlarsa “Sazakan Oynuyor”

claims.statement: Kuygorozh is a fabulous rooster-shaped being in Chuvash and Moksha mythology that brings treasure into the house.
claims.statement_id: Kuygorozh adalah makhluk ajaib berwujud ayam jantan dalam mitologi Chuvash dan Moksha yang membawa harta ke dalam rumah.
claims.quote: фантастическое существо в образе петуха в чувашской и мокшанской мифологиях, приносящее в дом сокровища.

claims.statement: According to belief, a rooster that lives six years lays an egg in its seventh, and carrying that egg in one's armpit hatches a kuygorozh.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, ayam jantan yang hidup enam tahun akan bertelur pada tahun ketujuh, dan telur itu bila dikepit di ketiak dapat menetaskan kuygorozh.
claims.quote: По поверьям, если петух проживёт шесть лет, то на седьмом году он сносит яйцо. Если положить это яйцо подмышку, можно выносить куйгорожа.

claims.statement: In some tales it can turn into a "flying fire".
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian cerita, ia dapat berubah menjadi "api terbang".
claims.quote: по некоторым преданиям, он может превращаться в «летящий огонь».

claims.statement: The kuygorozh constantly asks its master for work and carries out every task it is given.
claims.statement_id: Kuygorozh terus-menerus meminta pekerjaan kepada tuannya dan melaksanakan semua yang diperintahkan.
claims.quote: Куйгорож постоянно просит работы у хозяина и всё, что поручают ему, исполняет.

claims.statement: In Old Chuvash, kărăsh meant rooster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Chuvash kuno, kărăsh berarti ayam jantan.
claims.quote: В старочувашском языке Кăрăш - означал Петух.

claims.statement: The Tatar source calls it a fabulous creature that brings treasure into a Moksha home.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Tatar menyebutnya makhluk ajaib yang membawa harta ke rumah orang Moksha.
claims.quote: мукшы өйгә хәзинә алып килә торган фантастик мәхлукат.

claims.statement: A Yekyua or "mother animal" is a class of Yakut spirits that stay hidden until the snow melts in spring.
claims.statement_id: Yekyua atau "hewan induk" adalah golongan roh Yakut yang bersembunyi sampai salju mencair pada musim semi.
claims.quote: A Yekyua or "mother animal" is a class of Yakut spirits that remain hidden until the snow melts in the Spring.

claims.statement: Each yekyua is tied to a particular animal and acts as a familiar spirit protecting Yakut shamans; they are dangerous and powerful, the most dangerous attached to female shamans.
claims.statement_id: Setiap yekyua terkait dengan seekor hewan tertentu dan menjadi roh pendamping yang melindungi dukun Yakut; mereka berbahaya dan kuat, dan yang paling berbahaya melekat pada dukun perempuan.
claims.quote: Each yekyua is associated with a particular animal. They act as familiar spirits to protect Yakut shamans. They are dangerous and powerful. The most dangerous are attached to female shamans.

claims.statement: The kind of animal sets a yekyua's strength: dog yekyua are weak, elk yekyua strong; only shamans can see yekyua.
claims.statement_id: Jenis hewan menentukan kekuatan yekyua: yekyua anjing lemah, sedangkan yekyua rusa elk kuat; hanya dukun yang dapat melihat yekyua.
claims.quote: The type of animal determines the strength of the yekyua. For example, dog yekyua have little power, while elk yekyua do. Only shaman can see yekyua.

claims.statement: If one shaman kills another's animal, the shaman whose animal died also dies.
claims.statement_id: Bila seorang dukun membunuh hewan dukun lain, dukun yang hewannya mati ikut meninggal.
claims.quote: If another shaman who has manifested his animal kills the animal of another, the shaman with the dead animal dies.

claims.statement: When the yekyua fight in spring, their shamans fall ill.
claims.statement_id: Saat para yekyua bertarung pada musim semi, dukun yang terkait dengannya jatuh sakit.
claims.quote: When the yekyua are fighting in the spring, the shaman with which they are associated feel ill.

claims.statement: The strongest yekyua is the mammoth.
claims.statement_id: Yekyua yang paling kuat adalah yekyua mamut.
claims.quote: Najsilniejszy jest yekuya - mamut.

claims.statement: Yelbeghen is a many-headed man-eating monster in the mythology of the Turkic peoples of Siberia.
claims.statement_id: Yelbeghen adalah monster pemakan manusia berkepala banyak dalam mitologi bangsa Turkik Siberia.
claims.quote: is a multi-headed man-eating monster in the mythology of Turkic peoples of Siberia.

claims.statement: In the original myths Yelbegen was a many-headed dragon or serpent-like creature, which over time became a many-headed ogre-like giant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos aslinya Yelbegen naga atau makhluk mirip ular berkepala banyak, tetapi lama-kelamaan berubah menjadi raksasa berkepala banyak.
claims.quote: In the original myths Yelbegen was a multi-headed dragon or serpent-like creature ... but over time it evolved into other forms such as a multi-headed ogre-like behemoth.

claims.statement: Some epics feature many Yelbegen with different numbers of heads, children of Altan Sibaldai, "the golden witch", a follower of the underworld's lord, and name a Yelbegen king, Yelmogus.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa epos menampilkan banyak Yelbegen dengan jumlah kepala berbeda, keturunan Altan Sibaldai, "penyihir emas" pengikut penguasa dunia bawah, dan menyebut raja Yelbegen bernama Yelmogus.
claims.quote: Some epics feature multiple Yelbegen with different numbers of heads who are the offspring of Altan Sibaldai, "the golden witch", a cohort of the lord of the underworld. Some epics also mention a Yelbegen king named Yelmogus.

claims.statement: In an Altai legend Yelbeghen was a seven-headed ogre that took revenge on the Sun and the Moon and used to eat them.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Altai, Yelbeghen adalah raksasa berkepala tujuh yang membalas dendam kepada Matahari dan Bulan dan biasa memakan keduanya.
claims.quote: In a legend of the Altai, there was a seven-headed ogre, Yelbeghen, taking revenge from the Sun and the Moon, and used to eat them.

claims.statement: Ülgen shot arrows at Yelbeghen.
claims.statement_id: Ülgen memanah Yelbeghen.
claims.quote: The Ülgen shot arrows to Yelbeghen.

claims.statement: In some myths Yilbegän is described as a winged dragon, a serpent-like creature or an ogre-like giant riding an ox with 99 horns.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian mitos, Yilbegän digambarkan sebagai naga bersayap, makhluk mirip ular, atau raksasa yang menunggang lembu bertanduk 99.
claims.quote: In manchen Mythen wird der Yilbegän beschrieben als geflügelter Drache, als schlangenartige Kreatur oder auch als ogerähnlicher Behemoth, der auf einem Ochsen mit 99 Hörnern reitet.

claims.statement: Ajina is a demonic figure in the Turkic mythology of Central Asian peoples, especially Uzbeks and Turkmens and partly Tajiks.
claims.statement_id: Ajina adalah tokoh iblis dalam mitologi Turkik bangsa-bangsa Asia Tengah, terutama Uzbek dan Turkmen, dan sebagian Tajik.
claims.quote: демонический персонаж в тюркской мифологии народов Средней Азии, особенно у узбеков и туркменов, частично у таджиков.

claims.statement: Among these peoples it is common to frighten disobedient children with the ajina.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan bangsa-bangsa itu, ajina lazim dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak yang tidak patuh.
claims.quote: В культуре этих народов распространено пугать непослушных детей аджиной

claims.statement: Its look varies by place: a frightening humanlike being, a terrifying maiden or infant, a long-haired old woman, a horned red-eyed kid, or a frightening goat.
claims.statement_id: Wujud ajina berbeda menurut daerah: makhluk mirip manusia yang menakutkan, gadis menyeramkan, bayi menyeramkan, nenek berambut panjang, anak kambing bertanduk bermata merah, atau kambing menakutkan.
claims.quote: Внешность аджины разнится от места к месту. У одних она выглядит как страшное человекоподобное существо, у других как страшная дева, страшный младенец, длинноволосая старушка, козлёнок с рогами и красными глазами или страшный козёл.

claims.statement: According to some, the name comes from the Persian word janin, "embryo".
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian sumber, namanya berasal dari kata Persia janin, "embrio".
claims.quote: По некоторым данным, название персонажа происходит от персидского слова джани́н, которое переводится как эмбрион

claims.statement: According to others, the name comes from the Arabic word jinn.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber lain, namanya berasal dari kata Arab jinn.
claims.quote: под другим данным, название произошло от слова арабского слова джинн.

claims.statement: In folk belief ajinas live in abandoned, lonely places, ruined houses, dark dense forests and empty meadows and steppes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, ajina tinggal di tempat terbengkalai dan sepi, rumah runtuh, hutan lebat yang gelap, serta padang dan stepa tak berpenghuni.
claims.quote: По народному поверью, аджины обитают в заброшенных и малолюдных местах, в разрушенных и покинутых жилых домах, в густых и тёмных лесах, в необитаемых лугах и степях

claims.statement: The Uzbek source sees the ajina as a product of animistic belief in evil spirits.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber Uzbek, ajina dipandang sebagai hasil kepercayaan animistik tentang roh jahat.
claims.quote: Ajina yovuz ruhlar haqidagi animistik tushuncha, eʼtiqod mahsuli.

claims.statement: Qarakorshaq is an animal-like mythical creature in Turkic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Qarakorshaq adalah makhluk mitos mirip hewan dalam mitologi Turkik.
claims.quote: is an animal-like mythical creature in Turkic mythology.

claims.statement: It is said to hide in dark places, holes or empty houses to seize, carry off and devour its victim, but light and noise scare it away; it walks clumsily.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan bersembunyi di tempat gelap, lubang, atau rumah kosong untuk menyambar, membawa, dan memangsa korbannya, tetapi dapat diusir dengan cahaya dan suara; jalannya kikuk.
claims.quote: Qarakorshaq is described as hiding in dark places, holes or abandoned houses, waiting to grab, carry away and devour its victim; but it can be scared away by light and noise. It has clumsy gait.

claims.statement: Analysis of its traits suggests it may come from folk memory of real animals long extinct in parts of Anatolia.
claims.statement_id: Analisis ciri-cirinya menyimpulkan bahwa ia mungkin berasal dari ingatan rakyat tentang hewan nyata yang sudah lama punah di sebagian Anatolia.
claims.quote: Analysis of Qarakorshaq's attributes has led to the conclusion that it may actually derive from a folk memory of certain real animals, which have long since become regionally extinct in certain parts of Anatolia and are now known only in legend.

claims.statement: In Turkish it is called Karakorşak, an animal-like mythical creature of Turkic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Turki ia disebut Karakorşak, makhluk mitos mirip hewan dalam mitologi Turki.
claims.quote: Karakorşak (Eski Türkçe: 𐰚𐰀𐰺𐰀𐰚𐰗𐰺𐱁𐰀𐰚), Türk mitolojisinde yer alan hayvan benzeri mitolojik bir yaratıktır.

claims.statement: It has a clumsy or lumbering gait.
claims.statement_id: Jalannya canggung atau lamban.
claims.quote: Sakar veya hantal bir yürüyüşü vardır.

claims.statement: In Turkic folklore an Uylak is a male or female witch or spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Turkik, Uylak adalah penyihir atau roh, lelaki maupun perempuan.
claims.quote: Uylak in Turkic folklore is a male or female witch or spirit.

claims.statement: Uylaks are thought to be evil beings linked to the Devil, able to harm people by sending illness, killing cattle and spoiling harvests.
claims.statement_id: Uylak dianggap makhluk jahat yang terkait dengan Iblis dan mampu mencelakai manusia dengan mengirim penyakit, membunuh ternak, dan merusak panen.
claims.quote: Uylak are thought to be evil beings connected to the Devil. They are capable of harming humans by sending illnesses, killing cattles, spoiling harvests, etc.

claims.statement: Uylaks can change into animals and objects such as hounds, cats, coffins and even humans, and resist Archura's spells.
claims.statement_id: Uylak dapat berubah menjadi berbagai hewan dan benda, seperti anjing, kucing, peti mati, bahkan manusia, dan tahan terhadap sihir Archura.
claims.quote: Uylaks are capable of shapeshifting into various animals and objects; like hounds, cats, coffins, and sometimes even humans. They are also resistant to Archura's enchantments.

claims.statement: Uylaks pester and frighten people on the desolate roads they haunt.
claims.statement_id: Uylak mengganggu dan menakuti orang di jalan-jalan sepi yang mereka hantui.
claims.quote: Uylaks pester and scare people on desolate roads they infested.

claims.statement: The word Uylak comes from the Turkish verbs uylamak (to insist, pester) and oyalamak (to delay).
claims.statement_id: Kata Uylak berasal dari kata kerja Turki uylamak (mendesak, mengganggu) dan oyalamak (menunda).
claims.quote: The term Uylak comes from the Turkish verb Uylamak (means to insist, to urge, to pester) and Oyalamak (to delay).

claims.statement: The word can also be used as an insult.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini juga dapat dipakai sebagai makian.
claims.quote: Bu kelime aynı zamanda hakaret olarak da kullanılabilir.

claims.statement: Yunak iyesi is the bathhouse spirit of Turkic mythology; yunak means bathroom or bathhouse and iye means owner or possessor.
claims.statement_id: Yunak iyesi adalah roh pemandian dalam mitologi Turkik; yunak berarti kamar mandi atau rumah pemandian, dan iye berarti pemilik.
claims.quote: is the bathhouse (or bathroom) spirit in Turkic mythology. Yunak means bathroom or bathhouse, and İye means something akin to owner or possessor.

claims.statement: Every Caghlyk or hammam had an iye, a protector spirit called Caghlyk İyesi.
claims.statement_id: Setiap Caghlyk atau hammam memiliki iye, roh pelindung yang disebut Caghlyk İyesi.
claims.quote: Every Caghlyk or Hammam had an İye (protector spirit), that called Caghlyk İyesi.

claims.statement: If disturbed while washing, Yunak İyesi might pour boiling water on the intruder or even strangle them.
claims.statement_id: Bila diganggu penyusup saat mandi, Yunak İyesi dapat menyiram mereka dengan air mendidih atau bahkan mencekik orang yang lewat.
claims.quote: If disturbed by an intruder while washing, Yunak İyesi might pour boiling water over them, or even strangle the passerby.

claims.statement: Yunak İyesi could foretell the future: one stood with bare back in the half-open bath door, and he stroked the back if all was well or clawed it if trouble lay ahead.
claims.statement_id: Yunak İyesi dapat meramal masa depan: orang berdiri dengan punggung terbuka di pintu pemandian yang setengah terbuka, lalu ia mengelus punggung bila pertanda baik, atau mencakar bila akan ada kesulitan.
claims.quote: Yunak İyesi had the ability to predict the future. One consulted him by standing with one's back exposed in the half-open door of the bath. He would gently stroke one's back if all boded well; but if trouble lay ahead, he would strike with his claws.

claims.statement: Hammam iyesi was another bath spirit of Turkic mythology, akin to Yunak iyesi.
claims.statement_id: Hammam iyesi adalah nama roh pemandian lain dalam mitologi Turkik yang mirip Yunak iyesi.
claims.quote: Hammam iyesi was the name of bath spirit in the Turkic mythology. They were akin to the bathhouse spirit Yunak iyesi.

claims.statement: Among the Tatars the bathhouse spirit Muncha iyase is a mythical figure symbolising cleanliness.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Tatar, roh pemandian Muncha iyase adalah tokoh mitos yang melambangkan kebersihan.
claims.quote: Мунча иясе — татарларда чисталык символы булган мифик персонаж.

claims.statement: The washing place must be very clean; otherwise it begins to cause harm.
claims.statement_id: Tempat mandi harus sangat bersih; bila tidak, ia mulai mencelakai.
claims.quote: Юыну урыны аеруча чиста булырга тиеш. Шулай булмаганда, ул зыян сала башлый.

claims.statement: Vupkăn is an evil spirit of Chuvash mythology; vup means "to cast a curse, bring misfortune".
claims.statement_id: Vupkăn adalah roh jahat dalam mitologi Chuvash; kata vup berarti "mendatangkan guna-guna, membawa sial".
claims.quote: «вуп, воп» — «напускать порчу, приносить несчастье») — злой дух в чувашской мифологии.

claims.statement: Southern Chuvash believed the vupkan caused many terrible diseases, including epidemics and mental illness; it attacks as wind and corrupts the mind while staying invisible.
claims.statement_id: Orang Chuvash selatan percaya vupkan menyebabkan banyak penyakit mengerikan, termasuk wabah dan gangguan jiwa; ia menyerang dalam wujud angin dan merusak pikiran, sementara dirinya tetap tak terlihat.
claims.quote: Южные чуваши считали, что вупкан является причиной многих страшных болезней, в том числе эпидемий и психических заболеваний. Вупкан нападает на человека в виде ветра и наводит порчу на его ум. Сам вупкан остаётся невидимым.

claims.statement: Three black rams were sacrificed to appease the vupkan.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menenangkan vupkan, tiga domba hitam dikorbankan.
claims.quote: Для умиротворения вупкана приносили в жертву трёх черных баранов.

claims.statement: According to V. K. Magnitsky, northern Chuvash once pictured the vupkan as a dog and also blamed it for deadly epidemics among people and animals.
claims.statement_id: Menurut V. K. Magnitsky, orang Chuvash utara dulu membayangkan vupkan sebagai anjing dan juga menganggapnya penyebab wabah yang membinasakan manusia dan hewan.
claims.quote: По В. К. Магницкому, северные чуваши раньше представляли вупкана в виде собаки и также видели в нём причину губительных для человека и животных эпидемий.

claims.statement: If a vupkan settles in a house, the household declines into poverty.
claims.statement_id: Bila vupkan menetap di sebuah rumah, rumah tangga itu merosot dan jatuh miskin.
claims.quote: Если в доме поселяется вупкан, то хозяйство приходит в упадок, начинается бедность.

claims.statement: The vupkan can only be got rid of by cunning.
claims.statement_id: Vupkan hanya bisa diusir dengan tipu daya.
claims.quote: Избавиться от вупкана можно только с помощью хитрости.

claims.statement: The Chuvash source says a person struck by vupkăn stays poor however hard they work.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Chuvash menyebut orang yang dihinggapi vupkăn akan selalu miskin betapapun ia bekerja.
claims.quote: Вупкăн ерсен çын мĕн чухлĕ ĕçлеместь, яланах чухăнра пурăнать.

claims.statement: Abra and Yutpa are underworld serpents named in Turkic and Altai mythology.
claims.statement_id: Abra dan Yutpa adalah ular dunia bawah dalam mitologi Turki dan Altai.
claims.quote: Abra ve Yutpa - Türk ve Altay mitolojisinde adları geçen yeraltı yılanları.

claims.statement: They are two giant dragon-like serpents living in the Great Sea (Tengiz) of the underworld, resembling crocodiles.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya ular raksasa mirip naga yang hidup di Laut Besar (Tengiz) di dunia bawah, dengan rupa seperti buaya.
claims.quote: Yeraltındaki Büyük Deniz (Tengiz)'de yaşayan ve ejdere benzeyen devasa iki yılandır. Timsaha benzer görünümleri vardır.

claims.statement: They have forked tails and four legs, shining copper eyes and red feet.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berekor bercabang dan berkaki empat, bermata tembaga mengilap, dan berkaki merah.
claims.quote: Çatal kuyruklu ve dört ayaklıdırlar. Gözleri parlak bakır renklidir. Ayakları kızıldır.

claims.statement: They guard Erlik's palace and are known as his servants.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menjaga istana Erlik dan dikenal sebagai pelayannya.
claims.quote: Erlik'in sarayını korurlar, onun hizmetkarı olarak bilinirler.

claims.statement: They can swallow an elephant in one gulp.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dapat menelan seekor gajah dalam sekali telan.
claims.quote: Bir yağna'yı (fili) tek lokmada yutabilirler.

claims.statement: The South Azerbaijani source also names Abra and Yutpa in legends as guards of Erlik Khan's palace.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Azerbaijan Selatan juga menyebut Abra dan Yutpa sebagai penjaga istana Erlik Khan dalam legenda.
claims.quote: آبرا و یوُتپا، ائرلیک خانین سارایی نین گؤزتچی‌لری اولاراق دا افسانه‌لرده خاطیرلانار.

claims.statement: Al Ana is a deadly female spirit or demon of Turkic folklore said to live in thickets by rivers, streams and lakes.
claims.statement_id: Al Ana adalah roh atau iblis perempuan pembawa maut dalam cerita rakyat Turkik yang konon tinggal di semak dekat sungai, kali, dan danau.
claims.quote: is a female fatal spirit or demon in Turkic folklore. Al Ana was said to live in thickets near rivers, streams and lakes.

claims.statement: In some oral tales she is an ugly old woman with a hairy body, long straight hair and breasts so huge she washes her clothes with them, wearing a red hat with a fern twig.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian cerita lisan, ia berwujud perempuan tua buruk rupa, berbulu, berambut panjang lurus, dengan payudara begitu besar hingga dipakai mencuci pakaiannya, serta bertopi merah berhias ranting pakis.
claims.quote: According to some oral narratives, she took the form of an ugly, old woman with a hairy body, long straight hair and breasts so huge that she uses them to wash her clothes. On her head she wore a red hat with a fern twig attached to it.

claims.statement: Al Ana was said to steal newborn babies and replace them with her own children, changelings.
claims.statement_id: Al Ana konon menculik bayi manusia sesaat setelah lahir dan menggantinya dengan anaknya sendiri, anak tukaran.
claims.quote: Al Ana was said to kidnap human babies just after they were born and replace them with her own children, known as foundlings or changelings.

claims.statement: A changeling could be recognised by its odd appearance, disproportionate and often disabled body, and its wickedness.
claims.statement_id: Anak tukaran dapat dikenali dari rupanya yang tidak lazim, tubuh tak proporsional, sering cacat, serta wataknya yang jahat.
claims.quote: A changeling could be recognized by its uncommon appearance – disproportionate body, often with some kind of disability – as well as its wickedness.

claims.statement: In birth rites, though uttering its name is often taboo, many rituals concern the figure of Hal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam upacara kelahiran, meski menyebut namanya sering ditabukan, banyak ritual justru berkaitan dengan sosok Hal.
claims.quote: Doğum mərasimləri keçirilərkən, adının hallandırılması çox zaman tabu sayılsa da, istər-istəməz ən çox Hal obrazı ilə bağlı ayinlər icra edilir.

claims.statement: Arank is a water jinn in Turkic and Tatar mythology, also called Arang or Anank.
claims.statement_id: Arank adalah jin air dalam mitologi Turki dan Tatar, juga disebut Arang atau Anank.
claims.quote: Arank - türk və tatar mifologiyasında su cini. Arang və ya Anank (Anang) olaraq da deyilir.

claims.statement: They live both in and out of the water, are everywhere and rule the flow of waters.
claims.statement_id: Mereka hidup di dalam maupun di luar air, ada di mana-mana, dan menguasai aliran air.
claims.quote: Suyun içində olduğu qədər su xaricində də yaşayırlar və hər tərəf onlarla doludur. Suların axışına hökm edərlər.

claims.statement: They are well-behaved beings that rarely act badly and protect people.
claims.statement_id: Mereka makhluk yang berlaku baik, jarang berbuat jahat, dan melindungi manusia.
claims.quote: Yaxşı davranan varlıqlardır, nadir olaraq pis davranarlar. İnsanları qoruyarlar.

claims.statement: They help people about to die of thirst in the desert.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menolong orang yang hampir mati kehausan di padang pasir.
claims.quote: Səhrada susuz qalıb ölmə nöqtəsinə gələn kəslərə kömək edərlər.

claims.statement: The Turkish source also calls Arank a water jinn of Turkic and Tatar mythology.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Turki juga menyebut Arank jin air dalam mitologi Turki dan Tatar.
claims.quote: Arank - Türk ve Tatar mitolojisinde Su Cini. Arang (Arañ) veya Anank (Anang, Anañ) olarak da söylenir.

claims.statement: A similar being, the Yaran or Yeren, is a water jinn of Turkic and Altai belief that lives in water and generally harms no one.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk serupa, Yaran atau Yeren, adalah jin air dalam kepercayaan Turki dan Altai yang hidup di air dan umumnya tidak mencelakai manusia.
claims.quote: Yaran – Türk ve Altay halk inancında su cinleridir. Yeren de denir. Sularda yaşarlar. Genelde insanlara zarara dokunmaz.
